key_insight: PathFM moves beyond predicting only marginal quantiles and instead learns the full dependence structure of future trajectories. This makes forecasting more useful for path-level outcomes like cumulative demand, peak load, and event timing.
problem_solved: Most time series foundation models can estimate individual future values well, but they do not specify how those values co-vary across time. That leaves trajectory-dependent decisions under-specified, especially when the shape of the whole future path matters.
method: Uses flow matching to generate future multivariate trajectories directly, rather than forecasting each time step independently.
Models the joint dependence structure of future paths so downstream quantities derived from the entire trajectory are better captured.
Targets fast generative forecasting for multivariate time series while preserving path-level uncertainty.
impact: For practitioners, PathFM enables forecasts that are more informative for operational planning, risk analysis, and decision-making when aggregate or sequence-level effects matter. It is especially relevant in settings where standard point or marginal metrics miss important trajectory behavior.
visual_elements: Side-by-side comparison of marginal quantile forecasting vs. full trajectory forecasting

paper_title: PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting of Multivariate Trajectories
paper_authors: Jiachen Yao, Xiyuan Zhang, Annan Yu, Boran Han, Abdul Fatir Ansari
